title: Shellfs
subtitle: Read and write shell pipelines through file paths
intro: Use a shell command as a DuckDB file source or sink. A trailing pipe reads command output; a leading pipe sends COPY output to a command. Useful for local tools that already produce or consume CSV and JSON.

reference.name: 'command |'
reference.description: Read the command’s standard output as a file.

reference.name: '| command'
reference.description: Write bytes to the command’s standard input.

reference.name: read_csv(pipe_path, ...)
reference.description: Parse streamed CSV with normal DuckDB reader options.

reference.name: read_json(pipe_path, ...)
reference.description: Parse JSON emitted by a command.

reference.name: COPY (...) TO pipe_path
reference.description: Stream query results into a command; specify the format.

reference.name: SET ignore_sigpipe = true
reference.description: Optional setting to ignore SIGPIPE; default is false.

notes.title: Pipe placement sets direction
notes.body: Place | at the end to read, or at the beginning to write. Commands run through the host shell with the process’s permissions. Keep paths trusted and never construct commands by concatenating untrusted input.

notes.title: Treat the source as a stream
notes.body: Pipes do not behave like seekable local files. CSV and newline-delimited JSON are natural fits. Set explicit parsing options when needed, and ensure the command and any prerequisite tools exist on the host.
